source_title: I work in a hospital transfusion service - do we need to register with FDA?
locator: Hospital transfusion service description and 21 CFR 607.65(f) registration exemption
source_setting: U.S. hospital transfusion services performing compatibility testing and transfusion.
source_period: FDA web guidance accessed 2026-10-10; page does not specify operational study period.
value: compatibility testing
transfusion of blood or components
distinguish testing/transfusion service from routine collection or component processing
source_evidence_basis: FDA states that hospital transfusion services may perform compatibility testing and transfusion; it distinguishes services that do not routinely collect or process products from blood banks that do. Companion FDA computer-crossmatch guidance describes matching donor cells with recipient serum/plasma and SOPs to detect incompatibility.
limitations: This page addresses registration classification, not a complete specimen-to-issue SOP, turnaround time, emergency-release policy, or staffing. Local validated procedures and applicable regulation govern actual steps.
inferred_scenario_use: Include a blood-product request, specimen/compatibility work, availability/issue decision, and handoff as distinct events; model stock, test duration, and emergency branches only from target-site evidence.

assess home social support and arrange needed home services with the team/case managers

source_evidence_basis: AHRQ assigns case-manager collaboration for equipment and home services and describes care-team communication, social-support assessment, plan preparation/teaching, and information transfer.

source_evidence_basis: CDC lists infection-control professional activities, including surveillance, adherence monitoring, outbreak preparedness, prevention measures, communications, and feedback; it describes surveillance as systematic collection, analysis, interpretation, and dissemination.

source_evidence_basis: CDC explicitly recommends standardized terminal cleaning protocols by room type, pathogen/PPE considerations, ready-for-use identification, minimum cleaning times established by observation, awareness by patient-flow teams, and time tracking/audits.
